verses.english: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Once upon a time, mendicants, the titans marched against the gods.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed the godling Susīma,
‘Dear Susīma, the titans march against the gods!
Go, and march against the titans!’

verses.pali: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, susīmo devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā pamādaṁ āpādesi.
verses.english: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Susīma. But he fell into negligence.

verses.pali: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi …pe…
Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi …pe…
Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Sakka addressed the godling Susīma in verse:
without working for it or trying hard—
‘That a lazy man who does no work,
where a lazy man who does no work
that we might find the happiness
where one can live happily without working,
that surely would be extinguishment’s path!

verses.pali: So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṁ puññaphalaṁ upajīvamāno devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kārento uṭṭhānavīriyassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati.
verses.english: Since, mendicants, even that Sakka, lord of gods—while living off of the fruit of his good deeds, and ruling as sovereign lord over these gods of the thirty-three—will speak in praise of initiative and energy,

verses.pali: Idha kho taṁ, bhikkhave, sobhetha, yaṁ tumhe evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā uṭṭhaheyyātha ghaṭeyyātha vāyameyyātha appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
verses.english: you can excel at this, for you who have gone forth in such a well explained teaching and training can try hard, strive, and make an effort to attain the unattained, achieve the unachieved, and realize the unrealized.”
